description:
The committed family was single-valued - materializers/<tag> = {worker_id, node} - which did not merely ASSUME one materializer per shard, it ENFORCED it: any retirement predicate built on it ("the entry doesn't name me") makes a second instance for a shard suicide on startup. Bedrock intends multiple materializers per shard (settled with the user 2026-08-24): a distributor-class component seeing disproportionate traffic for a shard from one node may place an additional instance near it, or migrate one.

SHIPPED as PR #198. Shape: materializers/<tag>/<worker_id> = node.

POLICY DIVERGENCE FROM FDB, NOT MECHANISM DIVERGENCE. FDB's team size is fixed by the replication factor and its DD rebalances WHICH servers rather than adding one for read locality. But FDB's shard membership is already a SET (keyServers/<range> decodes to a team of server UIDs; the proxy addTags all of them), and its removal notice is addressed BY KEY (serverKeys/<victim>/<range> = false), never inferred from a single value naming someone else. The composite key with the member id in it, prefix-scannable with a minimal value, is FDB's own shape (SystemData.cpp:542).

ONE FAMILY WHERE FDB NEEDS TWO: keyServers is range-major for the proxy's routing, serverKeys is server-major so a server can find its own ranges and be individually addressed. Our notices broadcast on the shard tag rather than unicasting to a per-server tag, and a worker owns exactly one shard, so it needs no self-index.

TWO COLLAPSES THIS PRODUCED, rather than additions:
- The PLACEHOLDER became an ordinary member of the set. Parking therefore stops being destructive - it ADDS rather than overwrites - and can never destroy a live twin's entry. Retirement clears the departing member's own key and adds the placeholder in the SAME fenced commit when the shard would otherwise be uncovered, so the parked/degraded two-state dance collapsed to commit/retry/cede.
- The verification RESERVATION disappeared entirely: an extra materializer is now legal, so a concurrent recruit costs a redundant worker rather than a lost heal. That structurally removes the interaction behind PR #195's blocking audit finding.

READ-PATH SELECTION: covering_entry picks internally - real workers before the placeholder, then lowest worker id - so every proxy answers alike and a client's retry lands consistently. The client contract is byte-identical. That pick is now THE one pick (RoutingData.pick_member/1), shared by the proxy and the distributor, so locality/load awareness lands in one place (bedrock-q67.46).

MEMBERSHIP VS RESOLUTION: a worker's rejoin question under a set is "am I in the set?", not "is the picked one me?" - resolve_materializer became materializer_members.

MIGRATION: breaking format change, no dual-shape reader. Old single-key entries fail the decode loudly rather than reading as an empty family, which would silently re-recruit every shard and orphan the live ones.

DIVIDEND: with the victim named in the key, bedrock-q67.21.6's retirement predicate collapses to FDB's - act on a clear of YOUR OWN key - and the stream-replay hazard evaporates, since worker ids are fresh per recruit.
title: materializers/<tag>/<worker_id>: membership becomes a set
